name: Bisso Galeto
body:
Bisso Galeto CR
5

The body and head of this creature resemble a large rooster with a big red comb, but its wings sport long spikes and its tail is long and snakelike.

XP 1,600
N Small magical beast
Init +5; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision; Perception +13; Aura pollution (30 ft.)

DEFENSE

AC 18, touch 13, flat-footed 16 (+1 Dex, +1 dodge, +5 natural, +1 size)
hp 52 (7d10+14)
Fort +7, Ref +6, Will +5
Immune petrification, poison

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft., fly 20 ft. (clumsy)
Melee bite +9 (1d4-2 plus poison), 2 wing buffets +4 (1d3-2 +1d4 piercing)
Special Attacks lethal gaze, wing spikes

STATISTICS

Str 8, Dex 13, Con 15, Int 2, Wis 16, Cha 15
Base Atk +7; CMB +5; CMD 16
Feats Improved Initiative, Dodge, Skill Focus (Perception), Weapon Finesse
Skills Fly -1, Perception +13

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Lethal Gaze (Su)

A bisso galeto can kill with its gaze three times per day, directing its deadly glare at a creature within 30 feet it can see. The target is frightened for 1d6 rounds (DC 15 Will negates) and must make an additional DC 15 Fortitude at the end of its next turn (unless the frightened condition is removed) or die of fright. This is a mind-affecting fear effect. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Poison (Ex)

Bite—injury; save Fort DC 15; frequency 1/round for 6 rounds; effect 1d3 Con; cure 2 consecutive saves.

Pollution Aura (Su)

Water becomes polluted around a bisso galeto, and plants die. This works as the blight and pollute water witch hexes (Fort DC 15 negates), except it has no effect on animals and creatures.

ECOLOGY

Environment temperate plains and woods
Organization solitary
Treasure none

A bisso galeto is a variant of the cockatrice that is found in the valleys of Veneto. It lacks the ability to petrify its opponents, but its venomous bite and deadly stare are even more dangerous. Like its lesser relative, it is spawned from an egg laid by a very old cockerel and incubated by a toad (or a snake), except that the bisso galeto’s incubation lasts for seven years at least. The monster can also hatch in a farm from a normal chicken’s egg; when this happens, it can kill all people and animals around within mere minutes after its birth. Fields and rivers are polluted by the bisso galeto’s aura and plants rot around it.

These creatures appear to be a hybrid of bird and lizard or snake, with feathered upper bodies, a bird-like head with a wattle and comb, and scaly lower quarters and a long, serpentine tail. At first glance, one might easily mistake a bisso galeto for a cockatrice, especially since the two share both diet and habitat. However, where a cockatrice has bat-like wings, the bisso galeto’s wings are feathered, like a birds, save for the long, curving spines they bear, which are the creature’s primary weapon.

Bisso galetos are territorial, attempting to run off anything they see as a threat or competition. They use their magical ability to increase their size to frighten off opponents, or to increase their ability to fight, should the enemy not retreat when faced with a larger threat.

Cockatrice Killers As they compete with cockatrices for both territory and food, bisso galetos are hostile to cockatrices, often attacking on sight. A bisso galeto will typically win such encounters, being immune to the cockatrice’s petrification ability. Some creatures, particularly humanoids, will raise and train a bisso galeto, keeping it as a guard against cockatrices if they live in territory where such monsters are common.

Variants

According to some legends, the bisso galeto’s bite can influence the mood and personality of its victim, causing bad temper and mischeviousness. A bisso galeto gains this power when it’s spawned from an egg who was incubated for nine years rather than seven.

Such a monster replaces its poisonous bite with the following ability.

Emotional Venom (Su)

When a bisso galeto deals bite damage, the target is treated as if under the effect of an emotion ooze’s compel emotion ability (DC 16 Will negates). Every time the bisso galeto bites a creature, roll 1d6 to decide which emotion the victim will be affected from. An affected victim is immune to further effects of emotional venom as long as the effect of the previous bite lasts.
